mediterranean.name: Mediterranean
mediterranean.description: From Iberia to Mesopotamia, Gaul to the Sahara. Rome and Carthage fight for the Inner Sea. 24 larger regions with a focused network of routes.

europe.name: Europe
europe.description: From the Atlantic to the Urals, Scandinavia to the Mediterranean. Western Europe faces the Russian heartland. 28 larger regions with a focused network of routes.

americas.name: The Americas
americas.description: From Alaska to Tierra del Fuego, unite two continents across the Caribbean and the Andes. 28 larger regions with a focused network of routes.

africa_middle_east.name: Africa & Middle East
africa_middle_east.description: Cross the Sahara, follow the Nile and connect the kingdoms of Africa with Arabia and Persia. 28 larger regions with a focused network of routes.

central_asia.name: Central Asia
central_asia.description: From the Caspian to the Gobi, the great steppe heartland. The Silk Road empires clash across the roof of the world. 30 larger regions with a focused network of routes.

balochistan_borderlands_expanded.name: Afghanistan, Balochistan & Indus
balochistan_borderlands_expanded.description: Iranian and Pakistani Balochistan, Sindh, Pakistani Punjab and all of Afghanistan. Contest the Indus valley, Makran ports and mountain passes. 30 larger regions with a focused network of routes.

india.name: Indian Subcontinent
india.description: From Gandhara to Vanga, the Himalayas to Lanka. Ancient kingdoms, epic traditions and regional heritage shape this campaign. 30 larger regions with a focused network of routes.

southeast_asia_oceania.name: Southeast Asia & Oceania
southeast_asia_oceania.description: Island passages link the mainland, Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines with Australia and New Zealand. 28 larger regions with a focused network of routes.

waterloo.name: Waterloo · 1815
waterloo.description: Hold the ridge and farm strongpoints, or break the Allied line before the battle ends.

battle.name: Waterloo · 1815
battle.description: Hold the ridge and farm strongpoints, or break the Allied line before the battle ends.
battle.context: A focused reconstruction of the main battlefield. Prussian arrival, artillery and cavalry are abstracted into the starting forces; there are no scripted reinforcements.

sekigahara.name: Sekigahara · 1600
sekigahara.description: Fight for the valley road and the heights overlooking the route between eastern and western Japan.

battle.name: Sekigahara · 1600
battle.description: Fight for the valley road and the heights overlooking the route between eastern and western Japan.
battle.context: The core valley battlefield, with approximate encampments. Kobayakawa starts with the Western Army and remains loyal in this what-if scenario; defections and the distant Nangu forces are not simulated.

hastings.name: Hastings · 1066
hastings.description: Defend the English ridge or find a route uphill with William’s Norman army.

battle.name: Hastings · 1066
battle.description: Defend the English ridge or find a route uphill with William’s Norman army.
battle.context: Uses the traditional Battle Abbey location and a southeast approach. The extent and orientation of the fighting are debated. Ridge sectors refer to the terrain before the abbey was built.

hattin.name: Hattin · 1187
hattin.description: Contest the Horns of Hattin and the routes to fresh water during the Crusades.

battle.name: Hattin · 1187
battle.description: Contest the Horns of Hattin and the routes to fresh water during the Crusades.
battle.context: Covers the final approach from the plateau toward Hattin and Lake Tiberias. Water access is represented by objectives and supply routes; thirst, fire and historical troop totals are not simulated.

gettysburg.name: Gettysburg · 1863
gettysburg.description: Hold the Union fishhook or advance from Seminary Ridge across the fields of Gettysburg.

battle.name: Gettysburg · 1863
battle.description: Hold the Union fishhook or advance from Seminary Ridge across the fields of Gettysburg.
battle.context: A compressed July 2–3 scenario around the Union fishhook and Confederate approaches. July 1 and the distant cavalry battle are outside this scenario. Artillery and cavalry are abstracted into fixed strengths; assaults, reinforcements and day changes are not scripted. Sector control represents an approximate opening deployment, not exact regimental lines.
